stimulus.body: El fragmento siguiente sirve para comprobar la comprensión de esta forma. «This drink is prepared for winter gatherings and shared among friends, expressing warmth, hospitality, and festive tradition.» Cuatro opciones responden a él, y una sola concuerda con los datos de la nota.

questions.stem: Aplicando «Draft a cultural note / Connect to hospitality. / Writing a cultural note» al texto, ¿cuál de las opciones se sostiene?

answer.exemplar: This drink is prepared for winter gatherings and shared among friends, expressing warmth, hospitality, and festive tradition.

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: a cultural note should connect drink to hospitality and tradition. On that basis "This drink is prepared for winter gatherings and shared among friends, expressing warmth,…" is the supported choice.

questions.topic: A literary period and its concern

stimulus.body: En una nota de trabajo sobre este punto se lee: «Clarity, measure, and classical models.» « s costing sheet describes an era; which concern matches Neoclassicism? The chef » La nota ofrece cuatro afirmaciones posibles; solo una se desprende de lo que el texto dice realmente.

questions.stem: La nota se contrasta con «Name period concern / Clarity and measure. / A literary period and its concern». ¿qué respuesta queda respaldada?
questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: neoclassicism values clarity, measure, and classical models; the other concerns belong to other eras. On that basis "Clarity, measure, and classical models" is the supported choice. Option A ("Emotion and the sublime") fails because it confuses Neoclassicism with Romanticism; Option C ("Social misery and observation") fails because it confuses Neoclassicism with Realism; Option D ("Irony and pastiche") fails because it confuses Neoclassicism with Postmodernism.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: Author and work as historical fact

stimulus.body: El fragmento siguiente sirve para comprobar la comprensión de esta forma. «Eugene Ionesco, author of Rhinoceros.» Cuatro opciones responden a él, y una sola concuerda con los datos de la nota.

questions.stem: Con «Verify author-work pair / Rhinoceros play. / Author and work as historical fact» presente, ¿qué respuesta se desprende de la nota?

options.text: Jean-Paul Sartre, author of No Exit

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: rhinoceros is Ionesco's; Beckett, Sartre, and Camus wrote different works. On that basis "Eugene Ionesco, author of Rhinoceros" is the supported choice. Option B ("Samuel Beckett, author of Endgame") fails because it confuses two absurdist playwrights; Option A ("Jean-Paul Sartre, author of No Exit") fails because it picks an existentialist instead; Option D ("Albert Camus, author of Caligula") fails because it confuses author and work.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: A proverb in a sentence of the writer's own

stimulus.body: En una nota de trabajo sobre este punto se lee: «Every cloud has a silver lining, the note says.» La nota ofrece cuatro afirmaciones posibles; solo una se desprende de lo que el texto dice realmente.

questions.stem: Con «General truth.» presente, ¿qué respuesta se desprende de la nota?

options.text: Every cloud has a silver lining, the note says.

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: a proverb states general truth; option D does. On that basis "Every cloud has a silver lining, the note says" is the supported choice. Option A ("The timer reads five minutes") fails because it a measurement, not wisdom; Option B ("The bill is twelve dollars") fails because it an amount, not a saying; Option C ("The delivery is on Thursday") fails because it a schedule, not proverb.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: Order of composition in a short report

stimulus.body: El fragmento siguiente sirve para comprobar la comprensión de esta forma. «Research, outline, draft, revise, publish.» Cuatro opciones responden a él, y una sola concuerda con los datos de la nota.

questions.stem: El indicio de este ítem es «Order composition stages / Research first. / Order of composition in a short report». ¿qué opción lo cumple?
questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: a sound report moves research, outline, draft, revision, publication. On that basis "Research, outline, draft, revise, publish" is the supported choice. Option B ("Research, outline, revise, draft, publish") fails because it revises before drafting; Option C ("Outline, research, draft, revise, publish") fails because it outlines before research; Option D ("Research, draft, outline, revise, publish") fails because it drafts before outlining.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: Translating and preserving register

stimulus.body: En una nota de trabajo sobre este punto se lee: «Come on over, we'd love to see you.» La nota ofrece cuatro afirmaciones posibles; solo una se desprende de lo que el texto dice realmente.

questions.stem: Aplicando «Preserve register / Friendly and natural. / Translating and preserving register» al texto, ¿cuál de las opciones se sostiene?

options.text: You are cordially invited to attend.
Come on over, we'd love to see you.
Thou art invited to the feast.
options.misconception: treats "Thou art invited to the feast" as if it followed from the evidence

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: a warm invitation needs friendly, natural English; option B fits. On that basis "Come on over, we'd love to see you" is the supported choice. Option A ("You are cordially invited to attend") fails because it too stiff for warm invitation; Option C ("Attendance is requested") fails because it collapses to command; Option D ("Thou art invited to the feast") fails because it treats "Thou art invited to the feast" as if it followed from the evidence.
